evals.prompt: Describe assignments only; do not dispatch agents or edit files. Two independent component tasks own disjoint source files but both will edit docs/file-map.md and docs/known-issues.md. Explain which work can run in parallel and which edits must be serialized.
evals.expected_output: Run independent component work in parallel, but serialize edits to each shared document so workers do not edit the same file concurrently.
assertions: Independent source work can run in parallel.
Edits to each shared file are serialized.

evals.prompt: Describe coordination only; do not dispatch agents or edit files. Task A owns a parser and its area documentation. Task B owns an independent report formatter and its area documentation. Task C needs the completed parser from A. No files overlap. Explain the dispatch waves and execution mode while the user remains in conversation.
evals.expected_output: Run A and B in parallel background subagents, then start C after A completes. Keep the coordinator available for active dialogue.
assertions: A and B can run in parallel without serializing disjoint documentation.
C waits for A rather than dispatching with an unmet dependency.
Uses background subagents and keeps the coordinator available to the user.

evals.prompt: Describe assignments and communication only; do not dispatch agents or write files. Three implementation tasks need the same large-log investigation. A research note and a previous commit already provide most context. Explain how to fill the remaining gap and share findings without repeated investigation or copying the full context into every message.
evals.expected_output: Use one exploration subagent for the shared gap, reuse the existing note and commit, and communicate concise results through accessible context pointers.
assertions: Proposes one shared exploration rather than three duplicate investigations.
Reuses the existing research note and commit through context pointers.
Keeps communication sparse rather than forwarding complete logs or repeated context.

evals.prompt: Describe dispatch preparation only; do not dispatch or write files. One task is bounded read-only exploration; another is a substantive cross-file code review. All required task facts and runtime capabilities are available. Explain routing, how model and effort reach dispatch, and how runtime limits are chosen.
evals.expected_output: Load subagent-model-router once per agent context, evaluate a distinct route for each materially different subtask, submit its exact model and reasoning effort through dispatch controls, and assign each worker an effort-appropriate runtime limit.
assertions: Routes the exploration and substantive review as materially different subtasks.
Reuses already available router instructions rather than loading them again for the second task.
Submits the exact routed model and reasoning effort through dispatch controls.
Assigns every subagent a runtime limit based on expected effort and complexity.

evals.prompt: Describe procedure only; do not dispatch or write files. The user requires approval before dispatch. All task facts are available and no model preference was given. A proposed worker wants to spawn helpers, but nested delegation has not been authorized. Explain routing, the approval boundary, and the worker delegation policy.
evals.expected_output: Route using subagent-model-router without soliciting a model preference, honor the requested approval before dispatch, and prohibit nested delegation unless intentionally authorized.
assertions: Uses the router to select exact model and effort without asking the user to choose them.
Honors the explicit pre-dispatch approval boundary.
Prohibits nested delegation unless intentionally authorized.

evals.prompt: Describe coordination only; do not dispatch, send messages, or write files. A background worker has exceeded its assigned runtime limit but is still running. No separate failure or unsafe behavior is reported. Explain the immediate communication and whether lateness permits interrupting, cancelling, or replacing the worker.
evals.expected_output: Send a non-interrupting warning requesting status, completed work, blockers, and an updated ETA. Keep the worker running; the limit is a warning threshold and lateness alone does not justify interruption, cancellation, or replacement.
assertions: Requests status, completed work, blockers, and an updated ETA in a non-interrupting warning.
Keeps the worker running rather than interrupting, cancelling, or replacing it solely for lateness.

evals.prompt: Give an execution decision only; do not execute tools, dispatch agents, or edit files. The delegate-to-subagents workflow is active. A ready task is a one-line documentation edit with a known check, and the coordinator already has the context. No user restriction prevents delegation. Choose the executor and describe communication and dispatch settings.
evals.expected_output: Delegate the documentation implementation task, use sparse context pointers, and submit the router-selected exact model and effort with a runtime limit.
assertions: Assigns the task to a subagent rather than choosing local execution because it is cheaper.
Uses sparse communication and context pointers.
Uses the router-selected exact model and effort with a runtime limit.

evals.prompt: Describe executor choices only; do not run tools, dispatch, edit files, or commit. The delegate-to-subagents workflow is active. The parent coordinator has all context needed for a read-only Git status check and a deterministic commit of verified, explicitly authorized changes. Choose the executor for each operation under the active skill. Then explain what changes if the user says not to commit yet, or if unexpected files make commit scope uncertain.
evals.expected_output: Assign both the status check and the safe, authorized deterministic commit to subagents under the all-work-in-subagents rule, even though the parent has the context. A no-commit instruction blocks committing by every agent. Unexpected files require resolving scope before any commit; delegation does not authorize uncertain or unsafe commits.
assertions: Assigns both deterministic operations to subagents rather than direct parent execution.
Honors an explicit no-commit instruction for every agent.
Resolves uncertain commit scope before committing rather than treating delegation as authorization.
